newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges steady to firmer, one pct firm.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges steady to firmer, one pct firm.

text.p: European high sulphur barges were steady on Thursday in a very quiet market with buyers said sidelined awaiting prices to fall further after crude came off.
Low sulphur barges traded steady to firmer, high sulphur cargoes were offered steady to slightly higher while one percent changed hands at a good price with avails said low and buying interest seen.

High sulphur barges traded at $83 fob ARA twice for June in the afternoon after an earlier trade at the same level or $0.50 lower, while 1,000 tonnes of July fuel was done early at $83.75, a touch lower than Wednesday.
Late talk was $82 to $82/$83.50 for June liftings, traders said.
"It was a deadly quiet day, very low volumes. Crude came off and people were waiting to get better prices," one trader said.
"There's no real selling in July yet, I have seen one or two enquiries but all the trade is in June material still," one trader said.
Low sulphur barges were steady to a touch firmer. A very small parcel, 500 tonnes, sold for $97, but 5,000 tonnes was sold for $96, the level sellers have been insisting on for the past few days.
Later, most buyers were at $95 or $94.
High Sulphur cargoes were offered a shade higher at $81.50 cif after a cargo changed hands today at a higher number. But one buyer was heard at $79.
A Scandinavian refiner said he sold earlier in the day 30,000 to 40,000 tonnes at a floating price which he did not disclose but said was higher than his earlier offers of high fob plus $3/$3.50.
"High sulphur seems to be picking up, some people are trying to push it higher...But the upside seems limited given the large Russian programme," the seller said.
"I haven't seen any (Russian) cargoes there today but they're coming," he said.
One trader said one Russian cracked cargo was on offer at a steady two means minus $1.
Traders said one percent fetched a "good number", with a major refiner saying it sold 30,000 tonnes of low sulphur ex-Gottenburg loading July 1-5 at high fob quote plus $1.75 to an Italian refiner.
"They got that number as there's not that much avails around, only bits and pieces," one trader said.
A U.K. refiner was still offering its cargo at a steady to firmer $94.50/$95 and traders said it was not pressured to sell.
But one independent trader seeking one percent said that refiners' insistence on having fob instead of cif prices was delaying deals.

"We've bought some 200,000 tonnes fob over the past two weeks, but the freight rates are not being reflected. We told these guys they can sell to us cif if they want, but they want to sell fob," the trader added.
